roma-norte.name: Roma Norte
roma-norte.summary: Tree-lined, design-forward, and packed with some of the city's best cafés, bars, and late-night wandering streets.
roma-norte.famousFor: Famous for its Art Deco and Porfirian facades, inventive dining, and effortlessly stylish energy.
roma-norte.imageAlt: A Mexico City streetscape representing Roma Norte.

condesa.name: Condesa
condesa.summary: Greener, softer, and more curved than Roma, with parks, café terraces, and a slower Sunday-morning rhythm.
condesa.famousFor: Famous for Parque México, Avenida Amsterdam, and one of the city's most romantic walking atmospheres.
condesa.imageAlt: A peaceful scene in Parque Mexico in Condesa.

san-angel.name: San Angel
san-angel.summary: A cobblestoned historic quarter that feels quieter, older, and more painterly than the central neighborhoods.
san-angel.famousFor: Famous for colonial architecture, leafy plazas, and its Saturday artisan market around Plaza San Jacinto.
san-angel.imageAlt: A colonial-style street scene that evokes San Angel in Mexico City.

bazar-sabado.name: Bazar Sabado
bazar-sabado.summary: A beloved Saturday-only artisan market where the indoor courtyard feels more curated and the surrounding streets feel more lively and loose.
bazar-sabado.famousFor: Famous for higher-end Mexican craft, jewelry, ceramics, textiles, and one of the best souvenir hunts in the city.
bazar-sabado.imageAlt: Colorful market goods representing an artisan market like Bazar Sabado.

centro-historico.name: Centro Historico
centro-historico.summary: The grand historic heart of the city where plazas, cathedrals, palaces, and dense layers of history all sit on top of one another.
centro-historico.famousFor: Famous for the Zocalo, Palacio Postal, and some of the city's most dramatic architecture.
centro-historico.imageAlt: Historic architecture in central Mexico City.

chapultepec.name: Chapultepec Museum District
chapultepec.summary: A cultural corridor inside the city's great park where architecture, archaeology, and green space all share the same afternoon.
chapultepec.famousFor: Famous for the Anthropology Museum and some of the most important cultural institutions in Mexico.
chapultepec.imageAlt: A stately Mexico City museum facade evoking the Chapultepec museum district.

teotihuacan.name: Teotihuacan
teotihuacan.summary: An ancient city northeast of Mexico City where monumental pyramids rise out of the valley floor.
teotihuacan.famousFor: Famous for the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, the Avenue of the Dead, and some of the most monumental ancient architecture in the Americas.
teotihuacan.imageAlt: The pyramids of Teotihuacan under warm light.

days.title: Arrival & First Night Out
days.subtitle: Land, exhale, and let the city introduce itself after dark.
days.summary: The first night is built like a soft ignition: arrive, drop the bags, drink somewhere lush, eat the city's most beloved vegan tacos, and wander Roma until the night feels fully yours.
days.transportSummary: Airport to accommodation by car. Uber or long walk to Baltra in Condesa, then walking through Roma for the rest of the night.

events.title: Land at MEX
events.description: Welcome to Mexico City. Head straight to the apartment, leave the luggage behind, and let the trip begin in clean clothes and softer light.
events.editorNote: Private accommodation is roughly 25 minutes from the airport.

events.title: Baltra Bar
events.address: Iztaccihuatl 36D, Hipodromo Condesa, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: A botanical room, agave-forward cocktails, and exactly the right amount of glamour for your opening toast.
tips: One or two drinks is perfect here.
Keep the pace moving - dinner is part of the reveal.

events.title: Dinner at Por Siempre Vegana
events.address: Calle Manzanillo 66, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.travelNote: A short ride or walk into Roma Norte depending on energy.
events.description: Street-side, cult-loved, and gloriously unfussy. Start with the al pastor and let the city teach you its taco logic on night one.
tips: Order two or three tacos each.
Eat standing up and stay in the flow of the street.

events.title: Evening Wander
events.description: Walk Plaza Rio de Janeiro, Alvaro Obregon, and the quieter cross streets of Orizaba and Colima. No mission. Just arrival by atmosphere.
tips: Pause at the David fountain and watch the neighborhood move around you.
This is the most romantic way to meet the city.

events.title: Licoreria Limantour
events.address: Alvaro Obregon 106, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: The serious late-night cocktail stop. Glamorous, buzzy, and polished without losing warmth.
tips: Two cocktails is the sweet spot.
Walk home after if the night feels soft enough.

days.title: Markets, Museum, and the City's Street-Side Magic
days.subtitle: A Saturday built from craft, history, and mezcal.
days.summary: Saturday moves from a slow Rosetta morning to San Angel, onward to one of the great museums in the world, then back into Roma for street food, a moody dinner, and the choice between mezcal or dancing.
days.transportSummary: Three Ubers today: Roma to San Angel, San Angel to Chapultepec, then Chapultepec back to Roma Norte. Walking for the rest of the night.

events.title: Slow Morning with Panaderia Rosetta
events.address: Colima 179, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Pick up pastries and coffee, then bring them home. The morning bun and guava ricotta pastry set the tone beautifully.
tips: This is also the best window for any work catch-up.
Nothing important opens before 10 anyway.

events.title: Uber to San Angel
events.description: About 30 minutes south. The city changes character as you go.

events.title: Bazar Sabado
events.address: Plaza San Jacinto 11, San Angel, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Start in the juried indoor courtyard for the finest work, then drift into the outdoor street market for more texture, color, and movement.
tips: If something feels special, buy it here.
The best selection is in the first half of the day.

events.title: Uber to Museo Nacional de Antropologia
events.description: Roughly 25 minutes toward Chapultepec.

events.title: Museo Nacional de Antropologia
events.address: Av. Paseo de la Reforma s/n, Polanco, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: A two-and-a-half hour sweep through the Mexica, Maya, Oaxaca, and Teotihuacan halls. Monumental, grounding, and worth every minute.
tips: Do not miss the Sun Stone and the Teotihuacan context rooms.
This museum sets up Tuesday's Teotihuacan visit beautifully.

events.title: Uber Back to Roma Norte
events.description: About 15 minutes from Chapultepec back into the neighborhood.

events.title: Late Lunch at Jenni's Quesadillas
events.address: Colima y Merida, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Blue corn quesadillas pressed to order on the sidewalk. This is one of those only-in-this-city meals that people talk about forever.
tips: Order flor de calabaza.
Then get queso con huitlacoche.
events.backupPlan: If sold out, pivot to La Pitahaya Vegana nearby.

events.title: Rest & Reset
events.description: Back to the apartment to shower, breathe, and come back out feeling sharper.

events.title: Dinner at Los Loosers
events.address: Sinaloa 20, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Moody room, mushroom-forward menu, and a slightly theatrical intimacy that suits the evening.

events.title: Tlecan
events.address: Durango 200, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: A mezcal bar that takes agave seriously while still feeling alive and social.
tips: Margarita Texcoco
Tascalate Sour
Negroni Cacao

events.title: Mama Rumba if the Night Still Has More
events.address: Queretaro 230, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Live salsa, a small cover, and a joyful ending if cocktails want to turn into dancing.
events.editorNote: Skipping it is also a perfect choice.

days.title: Perfume, Rayo, and an Unscripted Condesa Night
days.subtitle: The city slows down, then turns luminous again.
days.summary: Sunday is built around one of the most distinctive experiences of the trip: creating a fragrance together, then dressing up for Rayo and letting Condesa handle the rest.
days.transportSummary: Two Ubers: Condesa to Centro Historico, then Centro back to the apartment. Evening is walking in Roma/Condesa.

events.title: Breakfast at Freims
events.address: Culiacan 99, Hipodromo, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Garden brunch, weekend ease, and a soft landing before heading into Centro.
tips: Share the ricotta pancakes.
Chilaquiles deserve their reputation.

events.title: Uber to Centro Historico
events.description: About 15-20 minutes from Condesa into Centro.

events.title: Quick Centro Wander
events.description: Step inside Palacio Postal, then let the Zocalo remind you how big this city can feel when it wants to.
tips: Palacio Postal is the don't-miss stop here.
The whole wander can stay short and light.

events.title: MUPE + Custom Fragrance Workshop
events.address: Tacuba 12, Centro Historico, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: A restored historic building, a museum devoted to scent, and the chance to blend a fragrance together that you leave with in bottle form.

events.title: Uber Back to Apartment
events.description: About 15-20 minutes from Centro back to Roma/Condesa.

events.title: Rest, Shower, Dress Up
events.description: Come back to the apartment, reset, and give the evening a sharper silhouette.

events.title: Rayo
events.address: Salamanca 85, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: The marquee bar moment of the trip: blind aroma box, agave-first cocktails, and a bar experience designed down to the last detail.
tips: Budget around two or three cocktails each plus a couple of plates.

events.title: Condesa by Night
events.description: Parque Mexico, Avenida Amsterdam, maybe food, maybe another bar, maybe just the walk home. This part is intentionally unclaimed.
tips: If you want one more stop, Departamento is the late-night rooftop option.
If you do not, the walk itself is enough.

days.title: Roma Norte All Day
days.subtitle: The neighborhood becomes the entire day, then your farewell night.
days.summary: This is the full Roma Norte immersion: breakfast, coffee, shopping, snack stop, long lunch, artisan market, and a night that closes the trip where it began.
days.transportSummary: All walking today. La Ciudadela is a 15-20 min walk from Roma — walkable, or grab an Uber if you're carrying bags.

events.title: Breakfast at Yerba Santa
events.address: Guanajuato 85, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Garden breakfast, herbal depth, and slow clay-pot cooking that gives the day a grounded start.

events.title: Coffee at Baveno
events.address: Orizaba 95, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Minimal room, good espresso, and a clean little reset before the wander turns into shopping.

events.title: Roma Norte Wander + Shopping
events.description: Utilitario Mexicano first, then the boutiques around Colima, Orizaba, and Alvaro Obregon. Let the neighborhood reveal itself in layers.
tips: If one gift sums up the trip, it is probably here.

events.title: Mercado Roma
events.address: Queretaro 225, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Snack, sip, and keep the appetite alive. This is a holding pattern, not the main event.

events.title: Lunch at Marmota
events.address: Plaza Rio de Janeiro 53, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Wood fire, Pacific Northwest-Mexican crossover, and the kind of long lunch that feels like the whole point of a Monday.
tips: Order the burrata.
Order the cauliflower.
Then follow the grill.

events.title: La Ciudadela Crafts Market
events.address: Balderas s/n, Colonia Centro, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: The city's artisan sweep: alebrijes, talavera, silver, textiles, masks, and the last big shopping pass of the trip.
tips: Bring pesos for the best leverage.
Walk the full loop before buying the first thing that charms you.

events.title: Freshen Up for the Farewell Night
events.description: Short reset, new outfit, and then back into the neighborhood for one last long evening.

events.title: Dinner at Cancino Roma
events.address: Plaza Rio de Janeiro 54, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Thin-crust pizza, trees overhead, and a terrace that feels almost European if you let the night soften around it.

events.title: Tlecan Return Visit
events.address: Durango 200, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: A mezcal goodbye. Return with context and order what you skipped the first time.

events.title: Chow Chow House
events.address: Orizaba 87, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Late-night energy if you still want another room, another drink, another hour.

events.title: Por Siempre Vegana, Again
events.address: Calle Manzanillo 66, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: The full-circle taco stop. Same sidewalk, same al pastor, four very different days later.

days.title: Teotihuacan + Speakeasy Goodbye
days.subtitle: Ancient pyramids in the morning, then one last precise nightcap.
days.summary: Tuesday belongs to Teotihuacan — walking the ancient grounds, taking in the scale, and letting the pyramids reset your sense of time. Then sleep, then one polished goodbye cocktail before the handoff to Puerto Vallarta.
days.transportSummary: Two Ubers: to Teotihuacan (~45 min) and back (~1 hr). Hanky Panky is in Juárez — walking distance from the apartment.

events.title: Uber to Teotihuacan
events.description: About 45 minutes northeast of the city. Leave early to beat the crowds and the midday heat.

events.title: Wander Teotihuacan
events.description: Walk the Avenue of the Dead, climb the Pyramid of the Sun, and take in the full sweep of the ancient city from the ground. Monumental, humbling, and worth every step.
tips: Bring water and sunscreen — there's very little shade.
The Pyramid of the Moon view looking back down the avenue is the money shot.

events.title: Lunch Near the Site
events.description: Grab lunch at one of the restaurants near the entrance before heading back into the city.

events.title: Uber Back to the City
events.description: About 45-60 minutes back into Roma Norte. Settle in, decompress.

events.title: Pack for Puerto Vallarta
events.description: Pack while the morning is still carrying you. Future you will be grateful.

events.title: Nap
events.description: Three hours. Non-negotiable. The evening works better if you actually surrender to the rest.

events.title: Hanky Panky
events.address: Turin 52, Juarez, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: An unmarked entrance, a dim room inside, and the last formal cocktail moment of Mexico City.

events.title: One Last Taco if Needed
events.address: Calle Manzanillo 66, Roma Norte, Ciudad de Mexico
events.description: Just enough time for one more taco and a final little ritual before home.

events.title: Final Pack Check
events.description: Charge phones, confirm the airport ride, set the alarms, then let the city go for the night.

days.title: Departure & Puerto Vallarta Teaser
days.subtitle: A quiet handoff from city rhythm to ocean light.
days.summary: Mexico City ends before dawn, but the honeymoon does not. This final panel should feel less like an ending than a doorway into the softer second chapter.
days.transportSummary: Quick early-morning airport transfer, then the short flight west.

events.title: Alarm
events.description: The final Mexico City wake-up. Quiet room, packed bags, and the low hum of departure.

events.title: Uber to MEX Airport
events.description: About 25 to 35 minutes at this hour. The city is almost still.

events.title: Viva Aerobus to Puerto Vallarta
events.description: Sleep on the plane, then wake up to the ocean half of the honeymoon.

practicalNotes.label: Currency
practicalNotes.value: Bring pesos for Bazar Sabado, La Ciudadela, Jenni's, and taco stands. Cards are fine in most Roma and Condesa stops.

practicalNotes.label: Transport
practicalNotes.value: The itinerary is built around walking within neighborhoods and short Ubers between them. Most in-city rides stay under 20 minutes.

practicalNotes.label: Tipping
practicalNotes.value: Aim for 15 to 20 percent at sit-down restaurants. A few pesos at taco stands is kind, but not required.

practicalNotes.label: Budget
practicalNotes.value: Cocktails tend to land around $12-$18 USD, dinners around $25-$50 per person, street food around $1-$3 per item, and central Ubers often under $5.

practicalNotes.label: Packing
practicalNotes.value: Tuesday afternoon packing is part of the itinerary on purpose so Puerto Vallarta begins easy.

closing.title: Next: Puerto Vallarta
closing.body: Mexico City is the appetite chapter - architecture, mezcal, neon, stone, rain on pavement, late dinners, and long walks through neighborhoods that glow after dark. Puerto Vallarta is the release. Salt air, a slower pulse, a different kind of closeness.
closing.teaser: You leave the city before sunrise, but you do not leave the honeymoon. You just trade boulevard light for water light.
